 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is now probable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Dealing with a sore right hip, Risacher was initially questionable for Saturday’s game. With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) out and Kyrie Irving (knee) downgraded to doubtful, Risacher may have more offensive opportunities. However, Naji Marshall is a better option for managers seeking a streamer.

 Naji Marshall, Max Christie, Zaccharie Risacher, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 The Mavericks won’t have Cooper Flagg or Kyrie Irving on Saturday, with the former facing an extended absence after injuring his shoulder during Friday’s win over the Pacers. As a result, Marshall and Risacher will start, with Naji offering a higher ceiling for fantasy managers seeking a streamer. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is available for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher is officially available for Saturday’s game. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving’s absences don’t guarantee more usage for Risacher, but his minutes may increase because of the injuries. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher had 11 points off the bench in Friday’s win over the Pacers. With the Mavericks’ lengthy injury report, he could play at least 30 minutes again, though he’s probably not worth streaming in most fantasy leagues. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher scored 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a steal, three blocks, and a three in 32 minutes against the Pacers. 
 He started the first half with 11 points and ended the game with 11 points. Risacher took advantage of all the easy opportunities in front of him. He got out in transition and took efficient shots. It seems like the Mavs are really prioritizing him and will get ample opportunities this season, even if it’s not a starter. Dusty May likes to play players with length, skill, and athleticism and Risacher can fit that. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) has been ruled out against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Martin will start the season on the injury report. However, Dallas has more than enough depth in the frontcourt to make up for his absence. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher may take on a few extra minutes. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Naji Marshall has agreed to a three-year, $52.2 million extension with the Mavericks. 
 Marshall is entering his third season in Dallas and is now set to be tied to the team until 2030. The two best scoring seasons of his career have come during his time with the Mavericks, and his veteran presence will be important as they continue to add young talent. Marshall has stepped up when Dallas has dealt with injuries in the frontcourt, and he’ll likely continue to be a valuable reserve option for them next season. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Zaccharie Risacher has been traded to the Mavericks in a deal that sends Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard to the Hawks and three second-round picks to the Thunder. 
 The former No. 1 overall pick wasn’t able to figure things out in Atlanta, but he’ll get a fresh start in Dallas. With Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz running the show for the Mavs, they have rebuilt this roster around Cooper Flagg by adding multiple new players in the frontcourt, including Risacher, Santi Aldama and Morez Johnson. Risacher’s role will likely be limited off the bench to start his tenure with Dallas, though a fresh start on a rebuilding team could yield him the opportunity to develop into the player the Hawks hoped he would become. The three second-round picks heading to OKC are Chicago’s 2027 pick from Dallas and most favorable picks in 2031 and 2032 from Atlanta. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #13 
 Naji Marshall (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the Bulls. 
 Marshall’s 2025-26 season has come to a disappointing end, as he missed the Mavericks’ final three games. The forward made 74 appearances this season, averaging 15.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game, which were all career-highs. He’s under contract for 2026-27 at $9.4 million and should remain a nice reserve for the Mavericks with occasional fantasy value when injuries hit. 
 Onyeka Okongwu 
 ATL 
 Forward-Center 
 #17 
 Onyeka Okongwu (finger) and Jonathan Kuminga (knee) are questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Okongwu and Kuminga sitting out Sunday’s regular-season finale would free up rotation minutes for multiple players. That includes Zaccharie Risacher, whose playing time has decreased with Kuminga in the fold, Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye. 
 P.J. Washington 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #25 
 P.J. Washington (elbow) and Naji Marshall (hip) are questionable for Sunday’s game against the Bulls. 
 Washington and Marshall are poised to finish the 2025-26 season on the bench, as both players are doubtful for Sunday’s finale. The former has missed the Mavericks’ last three games, and the latter the last two. John Poulakidis and Tyler Smith have played rotation minutes in recent games, with the former logging 30 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Spurs.

 Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
 Allen hasn’t started in place of Kon Knueppel (hamstring), but he has been able to fill the shooting void. That included a clutch four-point play in this game, which gave the Hornets a lead that they didn’t relinquish. Allen is rostered in just 33 percent of Yahoo! leagues, but with how many threes Charlotte shoots as a team, Allen should be rostered until Knueppel returns.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dennis Schröder lit up the Heat with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers on Saturday.
 After struggling in Friday’s blowout loss to the Hawks, Schröder was able to bounce back with his best performance of the season. Two of his three starts in place of Coby White (calf) have been productive, with the one poor performance coming in a 47-point loss that was bad for the entire team. Schröder is worth streaming until White returns to the lineup. He’s currently rostered in just 26 percent of Yahoo! leagues.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.
 Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.
 -  Noah Rubin

 With Yves Missi suffering a bone bruise in his knee during Friday’s loss to the Jazz, the Pelicans had a hole to fill at center. Instead of Derik Queen, Jordan will fill the void. While an interesting choice, Jordan offers better defense than Queen.

 Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.
 Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights. Any extra value he can add in other categories will just be a cherry on top.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Pelle Larsson provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (5-of-9 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Hornets on Saturday.
 After a rough start to the year offensively, Larsson was able to get things going in this one. He totaled nine points on 1-of-9 shooting across his first two outings, so this performance was a huge step in the right direction. Larsson was a late-round flier for fantasy managers hoping he would take a step forward for the Heat this season. He’s trending in the right direction, but he’ll need to produce to this level more consistently to be worth keeping rostered.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Bam Adebayo finished with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Saturday against the Hornets.
 It has been a rough start to the year for Bam, but after totaling 19 points in Miami’s first two games, he was able to surpass that mark in this one. It wasn’t enough for them to get in the win column, but it was good to see him have a productive outing. He’ll try to build on this performance in their next game, which comes against the Mavericks on Monday.
